source.citation: Joseph Kirkland, The Chicago Massacre of 1812, with Illustrations and Historical Documents (Chicago: Dibble Publishing Co., 1893). The whole book; the Appendix K letters alone are held at Joseph Kirkland, The Chicago Massacre of 1812, with Illustrations and….
what_it_does_not_supply: any document of 1812 from the factor or the surgeon's mate (those are in the War Department letters, read here only through Paul Dailing, 'The long death of Jean Lalime: A classic tale of Chicago…)
what_it_supplies: Mrs. Kinzie's account through Hubbard: Lalime met Kinzie outside the garrison and shot him, 'the ball cutting the side of his neck'; Kinzie stabbed him, hid in the woods and was later acquitted by the officers
Victoire Porthier's eyewitness account: sunset at the fort gate, Lieutenant Helm calling a warning, the pistol, the two falling together, Kinzie taken to Milwaukee by her father that night
the grave: 'in plain view from his front door and piazza' (Hubbard), a picket fence, 'two hundred yards west of the Kinzie house', and the bones found at Cass and Illinois streets on 29 April 1891
Lalime's letters of 26 May and 7 July 1811, and Main Poc's reply
